findings.title: Email automation-rule engine (Phase 9.4.2) is fully built but never invoked — every email trigger rule is dead on arrival
findings.evidence: emitEmailTriggerEvent (the sole entry point that loads matching email_trigger_rules, evaluates conditions, and dispatches) has exactly two references repo-wide: its own definition in lib/services/email-trigger.service.ts and __tests__/unit/services/email-trigger.test.ts. Grepping the whole repo for the function name finds no call site in any business-logic service. By contrast, its SMS sibling emitBusinessEvent (lib/sms/trigger-engine.ts) is called from 8 real production call sites: lib/services/outbox.service.ts, lib/services/mpesa-spine.service.ts, lib/services/mpesa-b2c.service.ts, lib/services/members.service.ts, lib/services/loans.service.ts, lib/services/contributions.service.ts, plus a backfill script and migrations' own inline SQL comments referencing it. outbox.service.ts (a real emitBusinessEvent caller) does not import email-trigger.service.ts at all. Meanwhile the full CRUD/API surface for AUTHORING email rules is live and reachable: app/api/v1/marketing/automation-rules/route.ts and its [channel]/[id] sub-routes (channel is validated to be 'sms' or 'email' in lib/services/automation-rules.service.ts's assertChannel) let an admin create, activate and configure an email_trigger_rules row today, including a template-existence check and frequency caps (Phase 9.4.3, memory: 'automation rules UI + admin edit CRUD').
findings.impact: An admin who uses the Phase 9.4.3 automation-rules UI to author an EMAIL channel rule (e.g. 'email the member when a loan is disbursed') will see it saved, validated and marked active with zero error — and it will never fire, silently, forever. There is no code path from any real business event (payment received, loan disbursed, contribution made, member joined, etc.) into emitEmailTriggerEvent. This is the same class of bug flagged in memory for Phase 13 ('dormant eligibility engine') and Phase 8 ('marketplace application form... 401'd since Phase 8') — a fully-shipped UI/API surface with no live wiring to its own engine — except here nothing has caught it yet because the feature produces no error, just silence.
findings.recommendation: Add emitEmailTriggerEvent(...) calls at the same call sites emitBusinessEvent already has (contributions.service.ts, loans.service.ts, members.service.ts, mpesa-b2c.service.ts, mpesa-spine.service.ts, outbox.service.ts), passing the same BusinessEvent shape both engines already share (lib/sms/events.ts's BusinessEvent type is imported by email-trigger.service.ts already). Add an integration test asserting that emitting a real event with an active email_trigger_rules row actually produces an email_campaigns row, not just that emitEmailTriggerEvent's own unit test calls it directly.

findings.title: marketing_campaign_sms_send has no orphan-recovery path — a permanently-failed job leaves the campaign stuck at status='sending' forever with no monitor, no 'failed' status, and no resend action
findings.evidence: handleMarketingCampaignSmsSend (lib/jobs/handlers.ts:1024-1058) calls smsService.sendBulkCampaign(...) and only reaches completeMarketingCampaignSend(...) (which is the ONLY code path that ever moves marketing_campaigns.status off 'sending') on successful return. sendBulkCampaign (lib/services/sms.service.ts:780) throws out of its own withAdminDb() block when reserveCredits() fails (`throw reserveFailureToError(reservation.reason, reservation.detail)` at line 869) — this happens for the ordinary, expected 'insufficient SMS credits / no billing account / inactive subscription' conditions, not an exotic edge case. approveCampaign (lib/services/marketing-campaigns.service.ts:312-368) enqueues this job with max_attempts:3 and no pre-check that the group can actually afford the send. On a credit-insufficiency failure, the job retries 3 times against the SAME deterministic failure (exponential backoff ~2/4/8 min) then is marked 'failed' in job_queue — but marketing_campaigns.CampaignStatus (lines 35-42) has no 'failed' member at all, so the campaign row is permanently stuck at 'sending'. lib/jobs/index.ts already has this exact orphan pattern solved for money-movement jobs (payment_orphan_monitor, disbursement_orphan_monitor, hourly) but no equivalent monitor exists for marketing_campaigns. grep of marketing-campaigns.service.ts for retry/resend/reprocess found nothing — there is no way to re-drive a stuck campaign short of a manual DB update.
findings.impact: The very failure mode the SMS trigger engine was explicitly hardened against (lib/sms/trigger-engine.ts:295-298: '[PROVEN-PROD]... payment.received rule... 100% "Insufficient SMS credits," zero of them ever going to reach a different outcome' — hence its 402/AppError special-case that fails fast instead of retrying) reappears unguarded in this newer Phase 9.2 job type. An admin approving an SMS marketing campaign for a group that is out of SMS credit sees the campaign hang at 'Sending...' indefinitely with no error surfaced in the UI, no automatic detection, and no self-service recovery.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) check credit/allowance sufficiency in approveCampaign before enqueuing (fail the approval loudly instead of the job later), or (b) special-case the 402/insufficient-credit error in handleMarketingCampaignSmsSend to call completeMarketingCampaignSend or an equivalent terminal update immediately instead of retrying, mirroring dispatchExecution's AppError statusCode===402 branch. Either way, add a terminal 'failed' CampaignStatus and either a monitor job or a UI resend action so a permanently-failed send is visible and recoverable.

findings.title: Email trigger rules' delay_seconds is validated, stored and shown to authors, but the email dispatch path ignores it and sends immediately — contradicting its own migration's documented design
findings.evidence: supabase/migrations/20260919030000_195_email_trigger_engine.sql line 38 documents the intended contract verbatim: 'Delayed actions: 0 = send inline, >0 = enqueue for run_at = now + delay.' The SMS engine implements this correctly (lib/sms/trigger-engine.ts:122-133): when rule.delay_seconds > 0 it calls enqueueJob('sms_trigger_fire', {...}, { run_at: new Date(Date.now() + rule.delay_seconds * 1000), dedup_key: `sms_trigger_fire:${executionId}`, ... }). The email engine's emitEmailTriggerEvent (lib/services/email-trigger.service.ts:244-272) does no such thing: it INSERTs the email_campaigns row with status='sending' unconditionally (line 246-251) and INSERTs email_campaign_recipients unconditionally (line 256-261), then merely increments summary.deferred if rule.delay_seconds > 0 (line 268-269) without ever deferring anything — there is no run_at, no scheduled_for consultation (email_trigger_executions.scheduled_for is written at claim time but never read back by any job), and no job enqueued. The existing email_campaign_drain job (already gated correctly per the 2026-09 audit's fixes) claims any row where 'ecr.status = pending AND ec.status = sending' with no time filter (lib/services/campaign.service.ts:291-308), so it will pick up and send these recipients on the very next 5-minute tick regardless of the configured delay.
findings.impact: This is secondary to the dead-wiring finding above (nothing calls this code path in production today), but it means the bug will surface immediately the moment finding #1 is fixed and any rule author sets a non-zero delay (up to 30 days per the validated range) expecting deferred send — e.g. a 'send 3 days after donation' nurture rule would fire within minutes instead. The reported EmailTriggerEmitSummary.deferred count would also misreport actual behavior to anything reading it.
findings.recommendation: Give the email engine the same run_at-based deferral SMS already has: either enqueue a new job type (e.g. email_trigger_fire, mirroring sms_trigger_fire) when delay_seconds > 0 instead of inserting the campaign/recipients immediately, or add a scheduled_for/run_at column path that email_campaign_drain's claim query respects.
